chapter: Soprano sax and working with Bechet
title: Working with Bechet on soprano and his temperament
summary: Rose says he gave Bechet a few soprano solos at concerts, and found him agreeable, simple and straightforward.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Did Bechet play soprano for you?
Well, I was only, I always gave Bechet two or three solos to do in a concert on soprano sax. They were strictly solos with rhythm accompaniments. But at all other times he played the clarinet.
He wasn't hard to control on that or anything? He didn't argue with you? Oh no, no.
There was never a problem with Sidney about programming.
A very agreeable kind of fellow?
Would you call him intelligent in his approach?

I would call him simple and straightforward. He always said what he meant, and you could always get a direct response from Sidney. You knew what he was going to do and what he wasn't going to do, and if he didn't like anything he'd tell you. And there were rarely any kind of situations where I ever saw Sidney having hard feelings about anything with anybody.
